title: Stephen: Verifying Sequencer-Aided Coordination Systems with Cross-View Prophecy
abstract: arXiv:2611.23811v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Many distributed systems achieve high performance by relying on dedicated sequencers to order requests, leaving replicas to commit them in that order. Despite more than a decade of such sequencer-aided coordination (SAC) systems, from Corfu and NOPaxos to LazyLog and SwitchBFT, their correctness has been argued only with pen-and-paper proofs or bounded model checking at the protocol level.   In this paper, we formally verify implementations of SAC protocols. The sequencer seems to make this easy: it decides the order of all requests, so the proof can place each request's linearization point at the sequencer using a well-known technique, prophecy variables. Yet a linearization point placed at the sequencer is not durable, because the sequencer orders a request before any replica commits it. Crashes and other rare events may trigger a view change that discards the request, nullifying the earlier decision and the proof that rests on it.

translated_title: Stephen：使用跨视图预言验证基于定序器的协调系统
translated_abstract: 许多分布式系统通过依赖专用定序器来对请求排序，从而实现高性能，各副本则按照该顺序提交请求。尽管这类基于定序器的协调系统已有十多年的发展历程——从 Corfu 和 NOPaxos 到 LazyLog 和 SwitchBFT——但其正确性此前仅通过纸笔证明或协议层面的有界模型检测来论证。本文对 SAC 协议的实现进行了形式化验证。定序器似乎使这项工作变得容易：它决定所有请求的顺序，因此证明可以使用一种众所周知的技术——预言变量——将每个请求的线性化点放置在定序器处。然而，放置在定序器处的线性化点并不持久，因为定序器在任何副本提交请求之前就已对其进行排序。崩溃和其他罕见事件可能触发视图变更，从而丢弃该请求，使先前的决定以及依赖于该决定的证明失效。
tldr: 本文提出 Stephen，通过“跨视图预言”技术首次对基于定序器的协调系统实现进行形式化验证，解决了定序器处的线性化点在视图变更时不持久、可能被丢弃而使证明失效的难题。
en_tdlr: Stephen introduces cross-view prophecy to formally verify implementations of sequencer-aided coordination (SAC) systems, overcoming the challenge that linearization points placed at the sequencer are not durable and may be discarded by view changes triggered by crashes and rare events.
